text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former oil minister Don Etiebet, who was detained after local council elections on Saturday, has been freed, aides say.
- Transport fares up 50 percent as petrol shortage bites; state oil firm says supply being normalised.
- State electricity utility firm NEPA says power rationing will continue, blaming the situation on inadequate distribution materials and debt of three billion naira owed by consumers.
- Central bank shelves plan to reduce number of banks that participate in clearing cheques to 12 from 46 after banks to be dropped say this will cause a run on their funds by depositors.
- Nigeria launches global campaign for its export processing zone in Calabar, southeast, with advertisements on Cable News Network (CNN).
- By-elections arising from last Saturday's local council polls will take place on April 3, investigations suggest
- Lagos state governor Colonel Mohammed Marwa and others unhurt after plane they boarded in capital Abuja for Lagos burst its tyres as it taxies before take off.
- Lack of cooperation from Britain's Midland Bank may have frustrated efforts of investigative panel to confirm whether or not state oil firm NNPC operates any secret accounts.

- Support for General Sani Abacha's government swelled on Thursday in Lagos, Abuja and Oshun states where locals held rallies praising his transition to civil rule programme and condemning recent bomb blasts in the country.

- Chairman of national reconciliation committee Alex Akinyele, receiving Britain's new deputy high commissioner (ambassador) to Nigeria, urges London to lift sanctions imposed on Nigeria and to support its democracy programme.
- Oil firms lobby for increase in Nigeria's budget for cash calls, the money government pays them to run the joint ventures that explore and produce the nation's crude oil.
